**Finding submitted — deviation (AUDIT), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations reviewed:** Paragraph 9 record-keeping and review regime (p0160–p0168), inspection of operations (10.8, p0177), and construction access (4.7, p0123). Only 9.8/9.9 create a right to review or audit *our* books; 10.8 and 4.7 are inspection rights of the system/Supply Contract, each at the inspecting Party's own expense, and are not audits of our usage.
- **Why it fails fallback:** 9.8 permits any Party to review or audit our cost records with no frequency cap and no notice; 9.9 only channels exercise through the F&ASC's own (extra-contractual) audit procedures, so it sets no notice or frequency floor. That is unlimited/unannounced audit territory.
- **Already met:** cost allocation is better than the fallback — the audited Party recovers its entire reasonable compliance costs from the requesting Party, with no underpayment exception, so no edit was made there.
- **Cure:** one inserted subparagraph 9.10 adding only the two missing fallback elements (once per year; not less than fifteen (15) days' prior notice), drafted symmetrically so our own reciprocal audit right and the favourable cost mechanic are preserved.
